source: Spec 124 R-DA (McDonald's Airtight V3): every entry is the measured PRE -> POST diff of docs/reports/golden/classify_coa_scope/{pre,post}/{coa,standalone}.json (Night A-swap 2026-10-22, lane COA-ASWAP, back-to-back under the dblock: PRE retaken on the LEGACY shell, the R-EQ shell swap applied, POST taken on the converted shell), explained from the descriptor deviation, register rule, runner code or the captures' own measured values it names. table_state was identical in all four captures (coa_applications, the single write target).

diffs.why: R-EQ shell swap: the legacy shell hand-printed JSON-log lines ("Loaded 35 trade configs / 805 logic variables from control panel", "Classification complete" with a context object) and a hyphenated completion line; the runner prints its own lines (the target line "database=postgres user=postgres migrations=<n>", the ledger-gate line where the step gates, the PIPELINE_SUMMARY and PIPELINE_META lines and one "[classify_coa_scope] completed in <DUR>" line). Log lines only: no table, counter or verdict value is read from them, and the PIPELINE_SUMMARY content is diffed separately in the summary.* keys.

scripts/classify-coa-scope.descriptor.json deviations[0] (Spec 124 R-DE (iv), O1 ruling 2026-09-21): audit_table.phase follows sharing.varies_by_chain.phase, the step's 1-based coa-chain index 6, generated by scripts/generate-sharing-phase.js; the legacy literal was 42 (the Spec 42 chain number).
The library stamps every declared check row with observed before_write / after_write (FLEET-2 lib #52); the legacy hand-built rows had no such field.

The library stamps every declared check row with source "check" and every compute context row with source "context" (verdict.js checkRow / contextRow); the legacy hand-built rows carried no source field.

The library renders the declared limit in force (e.g. "viol == 0", "pct <= 10") on each declared check row; the legacy rows carried the limit as prose or not at all. The bound is the step-owned variable in summary.records_meta.config.

Same metrics, same order; Measured ordering effect, not a behaviour change: the legacy PRE coa capture was the first scope run after the Night A-core coa run (and the 2026-10-22 coa feed refresh), so the legacy shell did the pending work (2,448 CoAs classified, 2,334 with a scope class); the converted POST then ran on that settled state, streamed nothing (the R-EX rerun proof PASS, zero writes on coa_applications) and read 0. The PRE standalone run, taken straight after, also read 0 and shows the same fixed point. table_state coa_applications is identical in PRE coa, PRE standalone, POST coa and POST standalone. Value moves on the coa capture: coa_processed 2448 -> 0, scope_classified 2334 -> 0, no_class 506 -> 0, no_project_type 245 -> 0, the percentage rows 4.7/95.3/20.7/47.6 -> 0.0 (an empty cursor reads 0, never N/A, legacy pin).

scripts/classify-coa-scope.descriptor.json: the legacy row unmapped_scope_count (a percentage printed as "4.7%") is renamed unmapped_scope_pct, the declared check id; the metric then reads the value the name says. Every other legacy metric keeps its name and order.

unmapped_scope_pct is a declared check (limit pct <= classify_coa_scope_unmapped_max_pct 10, severity WARN) and renders PASS in both; scope_classified_pct is a descriptive INFO field_coverage check in the descriptor, so it renders INFO on the settled POST where the legacy PRE printed PASS on its 95.3% (a value read, not a threshold change). Verdict PASS in both.

The converted runner owns the run ledger row on a standalone run (records_meta.ledger_row "owned"; the chain run reads "chain_owned" and writes none), so POST carries one classify_coa_scope row with status completed or completed_with_warnings (Spec 124 R-EQ, runner ledger ownership). Nothing is lost: the chain capture shows no row in either side.

#44 (g) one-way PRE -> POST (Spec 132 §core.14; R-DA §x-captures.3): the legacy PRE trace of the coa and standalone invocations did the pending work (2,448 CoAs classified) and so touched coa_applications.coa_type_class (reads); the converted POST plain traces are the settled fixed point (R-EX rerun proof PASS, zero writes), which streams no CoA and therefore touches no per-row column. Measured ordering effect, not a behaviour change.
